Digital Creativity I · I.5 Three-Dimensional Form

Recall check

Alone, from memory, 3 minutes. Then compare with a partner.

  1. At IHU, when is 3D prototyping taught relative to 2D?
  2. IHU 3D course halves?
  3. Name one item on I.5’s form-understanding evidence trail.
  4. Papahristou proves validated volume understanding — true/false?
  5. 3D prototyping: replace physical making or teach alongside?

Course geometric background · threshold · #c378606cc29b · Original course SVG

Timer: 3 minutes. Students answer alone, from memory, on paper; no notes, no slides.

Then 2 minutes in pairs: compare answers, then check the lesson.

Practice only: nothing is collected or graded. Five more questions with answers are on the unit practice quiz page.

Answers:

  • 1. Third year, alongside 2D CAD, after traditional patternmaking basics (Papahristou 2024, 5).
  • 2. Theoretical half and practical/laboratory half (Papahristou 2024, 5).
  • 3. 2D read before build; sketch→volume→digital sequence; or a divergence sentence.
  • 4. False — it reports structures/tool adoption, not validated volume measures (Papahristou 2024).
  • 5. Alongside — sequenced with 2D/physical literacy, not automatic replacement.

Ask: Which answer could you not recall? Re-read that idea before the Lab.

Digital Creativity I · I.5 Three-Dimensional Form

Exercise 1 · Flat → elevation → volume strip

Sketch flat → side elevation → simple volume for one garment region. Mark one ambiguity only 3D can resolve.

Three-sketch strip + one sentence naming the 3D test you will run next (no CLO required).

Image: Costumes civils HISTORICAL CLOTHING OF FRANCE civilian costumes male female dress fashion design c 1640-1925 Public domain French illustration Larousse du XXème siècle 1932.jpg

Costumes civils HISTORICAL CLOTHING OF FRANCE civilian costumes male female dress fashion design c 1640-1925 Public domain French illustration Larousse du XXème siècle 1932 · 19th-century French costume plate engraver · CC0 1.0 · Source

  • Timer: 20 minutes. Individual. Selected I.5 Lab — spatial craft feeding later cartel/workshop work.
  • Sketch flat → side elevation → simple volume for one garment region.
  • Mark one ambiguity that only 3D can resolve.
  • State what you will test in digital volume next (tool of choice; CLO not required).
  • Keep the three sketches as one strip.

Source: sequenced 2D→3D teaching structure in programmes (Papahristou and Zolota Tatsi 2024, 3, 5); steps are classroom adaptation.

Ask: Which plane lied first?

Digital Creativity I · I.5 Three-Dimensional Form

Exercise 2 · Silhouette from volume (not from polish)

Block the garment as 2–4 volumes, shade only mass, then trace the outer silhouette — compare to a flat of the same design.

Volume block + silhouette trace + flat comparison + one sentence on what the render would have hidden.

Image: Hand drawing on a graphic tablet.jpg

Hand drawing on a graphic tablet · Photograph uploader on Commons · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Source

  • Timer: 20 minutes. Individual.
  • Block a garment as 2–4 volumes (no surface detail).
  • Cast a single light; shade only mass.
  • Trace the outer silhouette; discard interior noise; compare to a flat of the same design.

Source: Classroom adaptation (silhouette-from-volume held — Moritz & Youn spatial visualization gap).

Ask: If the render looked “correct,” would your silhouette still match the flat?
